basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 14.' and it opens 'Vers. 14. Dilataberis ad orientem et occidentem. Quod Jacob terra promittitur, significat'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 14. Dilataberis ad orientem et occidentem. Quod Jacob terra promittitur, significat possessionem Ecclesiae Christo promissam. Per occidentem | interfectio justorum, per orientem exordium bonae conversationis; per septentrionem destructio et mortificatio peccatorum; per austrum vero fervor divinae charitatis ostenditur. In his ergo Christus regnat, et hanc gaudet habere haereditatem.
